The present petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus commanding respondent no.2 i.e., District Magistrate, Ballia, to decide the claim of the petitioner in respect of fair compensation for temporary acquisition of his land and damage caused thereby to the standing crops.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that he is the owner of Arazi Nos. 104, 105, 106 and 107 situated at Mauza Newari, District- Ballia.

It is alleged that the State respondents utilized Arazi Nos. 104 and 105, belonging to the petitioner for parking of vehicles during Dadri mela, resulting in damage to the standing garlic and cauliflower crops.

The respondents have not adopted any lawful procedure for temporary acquisition nor any notice was given to the petitioner and suddenly they occupied the land and destroyed the crop.
3. Pursuant to an order dated 11.03.2025, passed in the present proceedings an affidavit has been filed by respondent no.2, wherein it is admitted that the land of the petitioner of Plot No. 104 measuring 0.4660 hectare and Plot No. 105 area 0.4370 hectare, in which the petitioner has 1/6th share was utilized by the respondents during Dadri Fair in the year, 2024 as in the past.

It is stated that for utilizing the aforesaid land as well as adjoining land of various other tenure-holders, a proposal for temporary acquisition was sent to the Principal Secretary, Urban Development Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh.

entities.text: Urban Development Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is stated that by mistake the plots of the petitioner were left out from being included in the list of lands, which were to be acquired.

The Executive Officer of Nagar Palika Parishad, Ballia, after realizing the said mistake, vide communication dated 11.11.2024, made recommendation to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Ballia, to include the aforesaid plots also in the proposal for temporary acquisition so that compensation therefor is paid to the affected persons.
It is also stated that the Nagar Palika Parishad invited the land holders for settlement of compensation.

The tenure-holders raised demand for enhancement of compensation from the previous year and as a result whereof, the compensation amount which was Rs. 52/- per decimal in the previous year was enhanced to Rs. 54.6/- per decimal.
Accordingly, the total compensation for Plot Nos. 104 and 105, was worked out as Rs. 12,175.80/- and wherein the petitioner having 1/6th share would be entitled to Rs. 2029/-.
The said amount was paid to him on 28.03.2025 vide cheque dated 07.03.2025.
The list of tenure-holders, who have agreed to the rate as noted above has also been annexed alongwith the affidavit.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner admits that petitioner has received the cheque dated 07.03.2025.
He submits that the acceptance of the cheque would not mean that the petitioner has given up his right to claim fair compensation.
It is sought to be contended that the cheque was received on account of coercion.

5. Undisputedly, the respondents have utilized the land of the petitioner for few months during the fair and for which the petitioner is entitled to fair compensation in terms of Section 35(1) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (equivalent to Section 81 of Act 30 of 2013), as per the recommendations made by the Nagar Palika Parishad, Ballia.

Thereunder, the compensation is payable, as mutually agreed between the parties in writing, and in case of dispute relating to sufficiency of the compensation, the Collector is obliged to refer the dispute to the Authority.

6. In the instant case, the petitioner contends that his standing crop was destroyed and he is entitled to compensation for the same, therefore, there is genuine dispute between the parties relating to sufficiency of the compensation amount.
Consequently, in our considered opinion, the said dispute is required to be referred by the Collector to the decision of the Authority as provided under Section 81(3) of Act No. 30 of 2013.

The petition is, therefore, disposed of with direction to respondent no.2 to refer the dispute between the parties relating to sufficiency of the compensation amount to the Authority within four weeks from the date of communication of the instant order.
The Authority will endeavour to decide the claim of the petitioner expeditiously.
